meta.name: Terminal
meta.notes: Brand primary replaces the phosphor green: filled CTAs use --c-primary/--c-on-primary, while prompts, caret, prices and highlights use a lightness-clamped version (oklch) so even navy or near-black stays legible on the dark screen; accent drives status tags and labels.

issues: Catastrophic: every section below the hero (products ls -la, tree, story, stats, gallery, quote) renders as an empty void with just '~$' — content was hidden until IntersectionObserver fired with a -14% margin, so screenshots, fast scrolls and full-page captures show ~3000px of black
Hero typewriter is far too slow for long headlines: the Droogijs365 stress hero is captured mid-word ('snel en') with a giant orphan caret block on its own line
Caret was appended after the block-level accent span, so it always dropped to its own line, leaving a phantom empty line / big gap between headline and body text even after typing finished
Reserved headline height was measured before the VT323 pixel font loaded, inflating the hero gap
Kartstore logo (flagged 'light') has dark lettering that disappears on the black header
ASCII dividers are anonymous dashes; the section numbering lives only in a tiny corner tag
Creativity 7, typography 7, layout & rhythm 4 (empty voids), polish 4, brand robustness 7, mobile 5 (same empty voids), generic-template feel 6
fixed: Rewrote the section reveal: output is visible by default and only blanks for the instant its command is typed (triggered as soon as the section edge enters the viewport) — the 'run on scroll' signature is preserved but nothing can ever stay empty
Typewriter speed now scales with headline length so any brand's headline lands in ~1.6s
Caret is kept inside the segment being typed (text node + caret), so it hugs the last character and never orphans onto a new line or leaves a gap
Hero height is reserved only after document.fonts.ready (with timeout fallback), removing the phantom gap
Light-flagged logos get a hairline white halo so dark lettering stays readable on the terminal background
ASCII dividers now read '+--[ 02 ]------+', turning every section break into a numbered terminal frame
